ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $\angle B=30^\circ$, point $D$ is on the extension of $BA$, $\angle CDB=45^\circ$, point $M$ is on side $BC$, and quadrilateral $ACMN$ is a square. What is the value of $\frac{BM}{AD}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in Figure 1, draw $CQ\perp AB$ at point $Q$ passing through point $C$,\\
then $\angle AQC=\angle BQC=90^\circ$,\\
let $AQ=x$,\\
since $\angle B=30^\circ$,\\
it follows that $BC=2CQ$,\\
in $\triangle ACQ$, $\angle CAQ=60^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle ACQ=90^\circ-\angle CAQ=30^\circ$,\\
therefore $AC=2AQ=2x$,\\
therefore $CQ=\sqrt{AC^{2}-AQ^{2}}=\sqrt{(2x)^{2}-x^{2}}=\sqrt{3}x$,\\
therefore $BC=2\sqrt{3}x$,\\
since quadrilateral $ACMN$ is a square,\\
therefore $CM=AC=2x$,\\
therefore $BM=BC-CM=(2\sqrt{3}-2)x$,\\
since $\angle DQC=90^\circ$, $\angle BDC=45^\circ$,\\
therefore $\triangle CDQ$ is an isosceles right triangle,\\
therefore $DQ=CQ=\sqrt{3}x$,\\
therefore $AD=DQ-AQ=(\sqrt{3}-1)x$,\\
therefore $\frac{BM}{AD}=\frac{(2\sqrt{3}-2)x}{(\sqrt{3}-1)x}=\boxed{2}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the attached figure there are Figure 1 and Figure 2, and the problem uses Figure 1. Figure 1 shows that quadrilateral ACMN is a square, C is at the lower-left corner of the square, A is at the upper-left corner, M is at the lower-right corner, and N is at the upper-right corner; CB is a horizontal bottom side, and M is between C and B; A and B are on the same straight line slanting downward to the right, D is at the upper left of the extension of BA beyond A, and DC is connected. A right angle is marked at C in the figure, consistent with ∠ACB=90°. Then reason: According to the specified coordinate method, let the side length of the square be AC=CM=s. Take C=(0,0), A=(0,s), M=(s,0), B=(b,0). Because ∠ACB=90° and ∠B=30°, in right triangle ABC, tan30°=AC/BC=s/b=1/√3, so b=BC=√3s. Therefore BM=BC-CM=√3s-s=(√3-1)s. Since the direction vector of AB from A to B is (√3s,-s), its unit direction is (√3/2,-1/2), so the opposite-direction unit vector of BA passing through A toward D is (-√3/2,1/2). Let AD=t, then D=A+t(-√3/2,1/2)=(-√3t/2, s+t/2). From ∠CDB=45°, that is, the angle between vectors DC and DB is 45°. Starting from D, DC=C-D=(√3t/2, -s-t/2), DB=B-D=(√3s+√3t/2, -s-t/2). Let a=s+t/2, then DC=(√3t/2,-a), DB=(√3a,-a). Thus DC·DB=(√3t/2)(√3a)+a^2=3ta/2+a^2=a(s+2t). Also |DB|=2a, |DC|=√(a^2+3t^2/4)=√(s^2+st+t^2). Therefore cos45°=(DC·DB)/(|DC||DB|)=(s+2t)/(2√(s^2+st+t^2))=√2/2. Squaring both sides gives (s+2t)^2=2(s^2+st+t^2), which simplifies to 2t^2+2st-s^2=0. Taking the positive root, t=AD=(√3-1)s/2. Therefore BM/AD=((√3-1)s)/((√3-1)s/2)=2.

先描述图像：附图中有图1和图2，题目使用图1。图1显示四边形ACMN是一个正方形，C在正方形左下角，A在左上角，M在右下角，N在右上角；CB是一条水平底边，M在C与B之间；A、B在同一条向右下倾斜的直线上，D在BA向A外侧延长线的左上方，并连有DC。图中C处标有直角，符合∠ACB=90°。

再推理：按指定坐标法，设正方形边长AC=CM=s。取C=(0,0)，A=(0,s)，M=(s,0)，B=(b,0)。因为∠ACB=90°且∠B=30°，在直角三角形ABC中，tan30°=AC/BC=s/b=1/√3，所以b=BC=√3s。因此BM=BC-CM=√3s-s=(√3-1)s。

由于AB从A到B的方向向量为(√3s,-s)，其单位方向为(√3/2,-1/2)，所以BA经过A向D的反方向单位向量为(-√3/2,1/2)。令AD=t，则D=A+t(-√3/2,1/2)=(-√3t/2, s+t/2)。

由∠CDB=45°，即向量DC与DB夹角为45°。从D出发，DC=C-D=(√3t/2, -s-t/2)，DB=B-D=(√3s+√3t/2, -s-t/2)。设a=s+t/2，则DC=(√3t/2,-a)，DB=(√3a,-a)。于是DC·DB=(√3t/2)(√3a)+a^2=3ta/2+a^2=a(s+2t)。又|DB|=2a，|DC|=√(a^2+3t^2/4)=√(s^2+st+t^2)。所以cos45°=(DC·DB)/(|DC||DB|)=(s+2t)/(2√(s^2+st+t^2))=√2/2。

两边平方得(s+2t)^2=2(s^2+st+t^2)，化简为2t^2+2st-s^2=0。取正根，t=AD=(√3-1)s/2。因此BM/AD=((√3-1)s)/((√3-1)s/2)=2。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $\angle B=30^\circ$, point $D$ is on the extension of $BA$, $\angle CDB=45^\circ$, point $M$ is on side $BC$, and quadrilateral $ACMN$ is a square. What is the value of $\frac{BM}{AD}$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in Figure 1, draw $CQ\perp AB$ at point $Q$ passing through point $C$,\\
then $\angle AQC=\angle BQC=90^\circ$,\\
let $AQ=x$,\\
since $\angle B=30^\circ$,\\
it follows that $BC=2CQ$,\\
in $\triangle ACQ$, $\angle CAQ=60^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle ACQ=90^\circ-\angle CAQ=30^\circ$,\\
therefore $AC=2AQ=2x$,\\
therefore $CQ=\sqrt{AC^{2}-AQ^{2}}=\sqrt{(2x)^{2}-x^{2}}=\sqrt{3}x$,\\
therefore $BC=2\sqrt{3}x$,\\
since quadrilateral $ACMN$ is a square,\\
therefore $CM=AC=2x$,\\
therefore $BM=BC-CM=(2\sqrt{3}-2)x$,\\
since $\angle DQC=90^\circ$, $\angle BDC=45^\circ$,\\
therefore $\triangle CDQ$ is an isosceles right triangle,\\
therefore $DQ=CQ=\sqrt{3}x$,\\
therefore $AD=DQ-AQ=(\sqrt{3}-1)x$,\\
therefore $\frac{BM}{AD}=\frac{(2\sqrt{3}-2)x}{(\sqrt{3}-1)x}=\boxed{2}$
